resources.string: This phone runs the throughput service. It counts the bytes written to it and streams numbered notifications on request. Open Measure on another phone.

Connect to a phone that serves throughput. Each test runs at the default MTU of 23 first, then again after asking for 517. A packet carries the MTU minus 3 bytes of ATT header, and never more than 512 bytes, the longest value GATT allows.
On emulators the radio is simulated, so compare the rows with each other rather than with real phones.

resources.string: Connect again to measure MTU 23 again. Until then this connection keeps MTU %1$d
Every packet waits for the peripheral to confirm it, so each write costs a round trip.
Packets go out back to back and nothing confirms they arrived. The clock stops when the server\'s byte count comes back, and only that count shows whether any were dropped.
The peripheral pushes packets as fast as Android lets it, one notification in flight at a time.
